div.head: VIII Atr 37
div.ab: Ac on þam gemotan, þeah rædlice wurðan on namcuðan stowan, æfter Eadgares lifdagum, Cristes lage wanodan, ⁊ cyninges laga litledon.
Ac on þam gemotan, þeah rædlice wurðan on namcuðan stowan, æfter Eadgares lifdagum, Cristes lage wanodan ⁊ cyninges laga litledon.
Ac on þam gemotan, þeah rædlice wurdan on namcuðan stowan, æfter Eadgares lifdagum, Cristes lage wanodan and cyninges laga litledon.
Aber auf den Reichstagen nach Eadgars Lebzeiten, obwohl sie planvoll an berühmten Stellen stattfanden, schwanden Christi Gesetze und sanken des Königs Gesetze.
But at the assemblies after Edgar's lifetime, although they were held wisely at famous places, Christ's laws waned and the king's laws dwindled.
But in the assemblies since the days of Edgar, though advisedly they have been held in places of note, the laws of Christ have been neglected and the laws of the king disregarded.
But in the assemblies, although they took place designedly in famous places, since the days of Edgar, Christ’s laws have waned and the king’s laws dwindled.
But in those assemblies that met after Edgar’s lifetime, though wisely held in prominent places, Christ’s laws have been ignored and the king’s laws disparaged.
div.note: after Edgar’s lifetime: Wulfstan here alludes to the so-called Anti-Monastic Reaction, a period following the sudden death of King Edgar in 975 when the succession dispute between his sons Edward and Æthelred resulted in weakened protections for the Church and the withdrawal of many of the privileges religious foundations had accrued over the previous half century.

note.seg: Zu Eadgar s. o. 7; Einl. 9. Godes gerihta wanedan nu lange innan þysse þeode ⁊ folclaga wyrsedan ealles to swyðe, syððan Eadgar geendode, predigt Wulfstan 1014 p. 158, wahrscheinlich hierfür die Quelle.—Die in Urkk. genannten Reichstagsorte, auch kleine Dörfer, heissen inclytus; mein National assembly S. 43³.—Nicht etwa eine Trennung in weltliches Gesetz und geistliches Synodaldekret (wie Selborn Anc. facts 278. 346 meint, der solche in V. VI Atr unrichtig [o. S. 167 n. 2] findet) wird hier getadelt, sondern, laut 38, als Teilerscheinung des Verfalls von Kirche und Staat oder sogar als dessen teilweise Ursache, das Aufhören des Strafgeldempfangs durch den Bischof, der Geldverlust der Hierarchie; o. Einl. 12. Den Niedergang seit Eadgar beklagen Annalisten, Biographen, Kanonisten, Urkunden, gesammelt bei Plummer Saxon chron. II 164f.

On Eadgar see above 7; Introduction 9. Godes gerihta wanedan nu lange innan þysse þeode ⁊ folclaga wyrsedan ealles to swyðe, syððan Eadgar geendode, Wulfstan preaches in 1014, p. 158, probably the source of this passage.—The meeting-places of national assemblies named in charters, even small villages, are called inclytus; my National assembly p. 43³.—What is censured here is not, say, a separation into secular law and ecclesiastical synodal decree (as Selborn Anc. facts 278. 346 supposes, who wrongly finds such a separation in V. VI Atr [above p. 167 n. 2]), but rather, according to 38, the cessation of the bishop's receipt of fines, the hierarchy's loss of money, as one symptom of the decline of Church and State, or even as a partial cause of it; above Introduction 12. The decline since Eadgar is lamented by annalists, biographers, canonists and charters, collected in Plummer Saxon chron. II 164f.
Similar complaints are found in chronicles, biographies and other documents, see Plummer, Sax. Chr. ii. p. 164 f., and cf. Wulfstan, p. 158⁶.
